key_insight: A fully discrete model couples porous flow, viscoelastic deformation and frictional fracture contact, with proven discrete solvability, stability and a priori error estimates.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports reliable simulation of fractured porous materials where fluid pressure, deformation and fracture slip interact.
method: Represent fractures as lower-dimensional interfaces coupled to Darcy flow in the matrix and fractures.
Combine linear viscoelasticity with normal compliance and Coulomb friction at fracture surfaces.
Discretize using conforming finite elements in space and implicit Euler time stepping.
evidence_signal: A numerical experiment computes errors and compares them with the theoretical error estimates.
watch_item: The abstract reports one numerical experiment, leaving validation across complex fracture networks and realistic material conditions unestablished.
paper_title: Numerical analysis of coupled flow, deformation and frictional contact mechanics in a fractured porous medium
